body.heading: Make the sock
paragraphs: Roll a sheet of paper into a tube and tape it closed, or use a paper bag with the bottom cut off by your adult. Decorate it with bright colours and patterns.
Tape long streamers around one end. Tie string to the other end so you can hold it up high or hang it from a branch with your adult's help.

body.heading: Watch it dance
paragraphs: Take your wind sock outside. When the wind blows, the sock lifts and points away from the wind, and the streamers flutter and dance.
On a calm day, the sock hangs down sadly. On a breezy day, it flies proudly. The sock is telling you how strong the wind is without saying a word.

body.heading: Which way is the wind going?
paragraphs: Turn slowly in a circle holding your sock. The wind always pushes it the same way. That direction is where the wind is blowing to.
Airports and farms use giant wind socks for the same job. Yours is a pocket-sized version of a real tool.

takeaway: A wind sock points where the wind is going and dances harder when the wind is stronger.
safetyNotes: An adult should help with any cutting. Never fly your wind sock near roads or in stormy weather.
screenFreeExtension: Run with your wind sock on a calm day and make your own wind — see how fast you need to go.
